rated_messages.input_message: Imagine that your urge is a backseat passenger trying to distract you from reaching your destination. See if you can choose to keep driving instead of allowing your urges to distract you from where you want to go.
Ways of dealing with urges: play a game or an online quiz.
You don’t need to get rid of or change your thoughts about smoking—just let them pass by like a cloud in the sky.

Write down why you want to stop smoking to resist a craving. Remember, trying something to beat the urge is always better than doing nothing. Each time you resist a cig, you're one step closer to being tobacco-free.
Notice what is triggering your urge. Have understanding and kindness for yourself for feeling this urge. It isn't easy, but can you choose to let it be there without smoking?
Even though you are stressed, are you willing to sit with this urge until it passes if will help you break this habit?

Some people find it helpful to give a name to their urge. If you're experiencing regular urges, give that feeling a name ('Olga the urge'?), and tell it that you won't give in to it. It may make it easier to live with (e.g. "ok Olga, I need to be by myself now...").
Setting small goals when you feel unmotivated is best. Maybe a small goal for now is to breathe deeply for the next 3 minutes instead of smoking.
Feelings aren't permanent. They are always changing like the weather. Observe the storm that is coming, but don't fight it. Eventually the weather will change.
Each time you choose to not smoke after seeing someone else light up, you lessen the habit a little more.
